guarantees.claim: unused_data_out_q[i] is assigned the value of reg2hw.data_out[i].q for all i in 0..NumRegsData-1.
data_out_re[i] is assigned the value of reg2hw.data_out[i].re for all i in 0..NumRegsData-1.

assumptions.claim: The loop index range NumRegsData exactly matches the declared dimensions of unused_data_out_q and data_out_re.
assumptions.risk: If NumRegsData exceeds the array dimensions, out-of-bounds reads occur; if smaller, some bits are not driven, causing latches or X propagation.

uncertain_points.claim: The block reads back the .q field of a hardware write-only (hwo) data_out register (unused_data_out_q), even though the signal is named 'unused'. The comment suggests the design needed hwread access for re, but reading back output data may leak secret ciphertext.
uncertain_points.cond: Whenever reg2hw.data_out[i].q contains sensitive output data.
uncertain_points.risk: If unused_data_out_q is connected, even debug-logic, it could expose secret plaintext/ciphertext at the register readback path, violating security assumptions for hwo fields.

uncertain_points.claim: The loop bound NumRegsData may not match the actual bit-width of unused_data_out_q and data_out_re, because parameter usage is not verified against the signal declarations in this chunk.
uncertain_points.cond: When NumRegsData is set or derived from a parameter with a different value than the declared ranges.
uncertain_points.risk: Undriven bits in a combinational block may create synthesis latches or simulation X's, potentially masking functional bugs in downstream logic that uses these signals.
